mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.1% signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 0.1% triggers monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate deteriorating consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% signals labor market slack, reducing wage pressures and inflation expectations, which prompts accommodative monetary policy and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 105 indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO falls below 105.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST) above 1000 reflect strong residential demand, boosting related sectors and driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1000.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) combined with elevated federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.1%) signals persistent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% and FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
